title: It’s finally time to retire the word ‘podcast’
summary:
YouTube的2025年度回顾显示，我在该平台上收听时长最高的播客，竟然是塞斯·梅耶斯在《深夜秀》中的固定环节《近距离观察》。（《深夜秀》是美国CBS制作的一档电视深夜脱口秀节目，内容有音频版本。）如果放在去年，我可能会坚持认为这并不算播客，只算是电视节目的一个剪辑片段。但到了2025年，随着几乎所有主流播客都增设了视频版本，“播客”一词的定义已变得相当模糊。那种存在了数十年的传统电视脱口秀节目，如今与艾米·波勒的《Good Hang》、戴克斯·谢泼德的《Armchair Expert》、谢农·夏普的《Club Shay Shay》，以及Spotify播客榜单上的其他头部节目放在一起，几乎已经难以区分。事实上，它们现在同处于一个赛道。

来源：The Verge；作者：Andru Marino；原文发布时间：2025-12-24 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: According to YouTube’s 2025 Recap feature, the podcast I consumed the most on its platform was Seth Meyers’ recurring segment “A Closer Look” on his show Late Night. Last year, I would have argued that this is not a podcast. That it is, in fact, a clip of a TV show. But in 2025, with almost every major podcast now having a video component, the definition of the word “podcast” has become pretty meaningless. A decades-old TV show talk show format is now almost indistinguishable from podcasts like Good Hang with Amy Poehler, Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard, Club Shay Shay with Shannon Sharpe, and other shows at the top of Spotify’s podcast charts. In fact, they are now on the same playing field.
paragraphs.contentZh: YouTube的2025年度回顾显示，我在该平台上收听时长最高的播客，竟然是塞斯·梅耶斯在《深夜秀》中的固定环节《近距离观察》。（《深夜秀》是美国CBS制作的一档电视深夜脱口秀节目，内容有音频版本。）如果放在去年，我可能会坚持认为这并不算播客，只算是电视节目的一个剪辑片段。但到了2025年，随着几乎所有主流播客都增设了视频版本，“播客”一词的定义已变得相当模糊。那种存在了数十年的传统电视脱口秀节目，如今与艾米·波勒的《Good Hang》、戴克斯·谢泼德的《Armchair Expert》、谢农·夏普的《Club Shay Shay》，以及Spotify播客榜单上的其他头部节目放在一起，几乎已经难以区分。事实上，它们现在同处于一个赛道。

paragraphs.contentEn: Scrolling though my YouTube feed, most of the suggestions in the Podcast tab are late-night talk show interviews, host-driven video essays, food reviews, and cable news segments — very far from what we used to use the term for: narrative audio journalism and roundtable discussions. So in 2026, instead of trying to define what a podcast is, I think we need to stop using the word altogether. “Podcast” is becoming an outdated or even a potentially cringe internet relic, similar to how the phrase “web series” faded from use online.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在浏览YouTube首页推荐时，我注意到，播客栏目下出现的大多是深夜脱口秀的访谈片段、主持人主导的深度视频解析、美食评测以及有线电视新闻的剪辑片段——这些内容与我们过去所理解的播客形态（即叙事性的音频新闻和圆桌式讨论）已相去甚远。因此，到了2026年，与其继续纠结如何定义播客，不如彻底摒弃这个词。“播客”正逐渐沦为一个过时、甚至略显尴尬的互联网遗留概念，就像当年的“网剧”一词，在网络语境中也逐渐无人再提了。

paragraphs.contentEn: So what do we call these formats instead? I don’t think we’re going to invent a new word, but instead repurpose an old one. Bloomberg’s Ashley Carman noticed this change in her coverage of The Podcast Show in London this past May: ...two separate panelists made it clear they do not call their podcasts “podcasts.” Georgie Holt, chief executive at FlightStory, the company behind Steven Bartlett’s Diary of a CEO , said the team calls their programming “shows.” In a conversation on stage with me, Max Cutler, founder of Pave Studios, said exactly the same thing.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，我们该如何称呼这类内容形态？我认为，我们未必会创造一个新词，更可能是赋予一个旧词新的含义。彭博社记者阿什利·卡曼在今年5月报道伦敦“播客展”时，就注意到了这一变化：……有两位嘉宾不约而同地明确表示，他们不称自己的作品为“播客”。史蒂文·巴特利特旗下播客《CEO日记》背后的制作公司FlightStory，其首席执行官乔治·霍尔特表示，团队内部将这类内容统一称为“节目”。而在台上接受卡曼采访时，Pave Studios创始人马克斯·卡特勒也表达了完全一致的观点。

paragraphs.contentEn: Anecdotally I have heard this change of nomenclature from “podcasts” to “shows” internally here at Vox Media too, and echoed from my colleagues at other media companies as well. Using the word “show” seems to be a more marketable term for advertising, especially when attaching celebrity names to the project. Pitching podcasts to advertisers sounds limiting and niche, but pitching a “show” — hey, that’s a place where they can get ears and eyes, and a definitive platform where the shows will live. Podcast creators want that Seth Meyers money. Because of this, fans will likely begin calling them “shows” as well, the same way consumers started claiming internal marketing terms like “influencers” and “creators.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 据我了解，在Vox Media内部，也出现了从“播客”到“节目”的称呼转变，我在其他媒体公司的同行那里也听到了同样的说法。使用“节目”这一说法，在向广告商推销时似乎更具卖点，特别是在项目有名人背书的情况下。向广告主推介播客往往显得受众有限、定位偏窄；但推介一档“节目”——嘿，那是一个能同时吸引听众与观众的内容载体，而且还有一个明确的发布平台。播客创作者们希望获得的是塞斯·梅耶斯（电视脱口秀主持人）那种商业回报。正因如此，听众很可能也会慢慢改口，开始称它们为“节目”，就像消费者当年逐渐接受了“网红”、“创作者”这些原本属于内部的营销术语一样。

paragraphs.contentEn: We’re seeing the word fade from the hosts, too. There’s a recurring bit on The Adam Friedland Show now where guests call the show a podcast, and the titular host corrects them instantly, claiming it’s a talk show. Instead of the cliche “Find us wherever you get podcasts” sign-off, I’ve noticed many hosts are now pivoting more to the “like-and-subscribe” phrasing of YouTube culture. These podcast shows are all starting to live together with non-podcast shows like Hot Ones, Chicken Shop Date, the Criterion Closet series, Tonight Show clips, etc. — so why limit them to a term that used to go hand-in-hand with iPods?
paragraphs.contentZh: 我们也能从主持人的用语中，看到播客一词正在淡出。在《亚当·弗里德兰秀》中，如今有一个反复出现的桥段：当嘉宾称这档节目为播客时，主持人亚当·弗里德兰会立刻予以纠正，强调这是一档脱口秀节目。与此同时，我注意到，许多主持人已不再使用“在各大播客平台收听我们”这一程式化的结尾语，而是采用更具YouTube特色的“点赞并订阅”来收尾。这些原本被归入播客范畴的节目，如今正与《Hot Ones》、《Chicken Shop Date》、“Criterion Closet” 系列以及《今夜秀》切片等非播客内容，共同存在于同一内容生态之中——既然如此，为什么还要继续用一个曾与iPod绑定的过时术语来界定它们？

paragraphs.contentEn: Unfortunately, all this also means that a lot of the openness of podcasting is slowly going away and becoming more centralized on platforms like YouTube and Netflix. YouTube says more than one billion people watch podcasts on its platform every month. It was reported by Bloomberg that Netflix is going to add podcasts to its streaming platform, developing its own shows and working with major networks like Spotify, iHeartMedia, and Sirius.
paragraphs.contentZh: 但遗憾的是，这一系列变化也意味着播客原本相对开放的生态正在逐渐收缩，内容分发正越来越多地集中到YouTube、Netflix等大型平台之上。YouTube宣称，每月有超过10亿用户在其平台上观看播客内容。另据彭博社报道，Netflix计划将播客纳入其流媒体体系，既开发自制节目，也将与Spotify、iHeartMedia、Sirius等主流音频内容商合作。

paragraphs.contentEn: In fact, YouTube is starting to look more like Netflix. “Talk show–style podcasts” on YouTube are already considered to be the next generation of late night TV, especially with CBS signaling an end to investing in the genre by cancelling The Late Show with Stephen Colbert in 2026 (I can imagine a cheaper-made podcast going into CBS’s late night lineup instead) and celebrity press tours prioritizing YouTube over traditional network TV. Next year, you probably won’t be recommending your favorite new podcast to your friend, but instead something you “watched on TV.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 事实上，如今的YouTube越来越呈现出类似Netflix的平台形态。YouTube上的“脱口秀式播客”已被不少业内人士视为新一代的深夜电视节目，一个明显的信号是，哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）正在减少对深夜电视节目的投入，并计划于2026年停播《斯蒂芬·科尔伯特晚间秀》（可以想见，未来CBS的深夜时段将让位给制作成本更低的播客节目）；同时，明星宣传行程也优先选择YouTube，而非传统电视网。在这样的背景下，到了明年，你向朋友推荐的或许不再是某档新“播客”，而会是某个你“在电视上看过”的节目。

paragraphs.contentEn: Despite all this, I still think the audio-only format will stick around. After all, people still drive cars, and they aren’t typically looking at a screen for the whole three hours of a podcast. In fact, according to Edison Research, most podcast listening is done at home. It’s likely, though, that most audio-only podcasts will be from more independently run shows. Media companies will still publish audio versions of their video shows for the podcatcher apps, but they’re not the priority anymore. As a result (and long overdue from the era of the iPod), I think the era of the term “podcast” is ending. Perhaps in the future, the question “What is a podcast?” will disappear in favor of “What was a podcast?”
paragraphs.contentZh: 尽管如此，我仍认为纯音频的内容形态不会消失。毕竟，人们依然需要驾车出行，也无法在收听长达数小时的播客时一直盯着屏幕。事实上，爱迪生研究公司的数据显示，大多数播客是在家中收听的。不过可以预见的是，未来坚持纯音频形式的播客，更多将来自独立运营的节目。媒体机构仍会将视频节目的音频版本发布到各类播客客户端，但这已不再是它们的核心重点。因此，我认为“播客”这一术语本身正走向终结（这其实是早在iPod时代落幕时就该发生的变化）。或许在不久的将来，人们不会再问“什么是播客？”，而是会好奇：“播客，曾经是什么？”
